For reference to the use of doxycycline in the management of various musculoskele- tal and joint disorders, see under Tetracycline, p.350. Onchocerciasis. As in lymphatic filariasis (above), Onchocer- ca volvulus worms rely on a symbiotic relationship with Wol- bachia endobacteria, and this has provided a new approach in the treatment of individuals with onchocerciasis ( p.137). A 4-month controlled clinical study1 of 35 patients with onchocerciasis found that those given oral doxycycline 100 mg daily for 6 weeks showed a trend toward more frequent degeneration or death of adult worms and suppressed embryonic development at early stages for the duration of the study period. A subsequent study2 of 88 patients found that embryogenesis was interrupted for at least 18 months in those given a single standard dose of ivermectin (150 micrograms/kg) plus oral doxycycline 100 mg daily for 6 weeks compared to those given only the standard dose of ivermectin. 1.
